overview: 36 official Group 1 Qs (2008–2024) on economic geography: crops and agricultural regions (14), fuel and power (6), mineral-based industry (5), transport (4) and a few agro/industry/trade items. Older papers asked 'which place/state produces X'; 2023–24 favour match lists (crops, shifting-cultivation names, industry centres, geographers) and statement items on steel, sugarcane, oil fields and railways. Production-rank keys are time-sensitive and some were contested.

possibility.what_they_ask: leading state/country for a crop, transplanted crops, IR-8, sugarcane climate, wheat regions, shifting-cultivation names by region, agricultural regionalisation and the geographers behind each method, AP district crop facts (coffee agencies, food-crop area)
industry → centre match (Jamshedpur, Kolkata, Barauni, Perambur), woollen regions of the UK, tourism-sector facts
which industry is not agro-based, silk type → state, location of jute mills

possibility.angle: Mineral-based industries – iron and steel, cement, tin
possibility.what_they_ask: steel regions of the world, India's steel rank, steel or smelting centres abroad, cement plant → district in AP

possibility.evidence: 0 official Qs (paper appears only as an agro-based option in 2008)
possibility.what_they_ask: natural targets by analogy: paper and pulp centres (e.g. Rajahmundry, Sirpur), raw materials (bamboo, softwood), lac, sericulture forest silks

possibility.angle: Fuel and power-based industries – oil, gas, thermal power
possibility.what_they_ask: oil-field locations (Assam vs Gujarat), refinery places, LPG composition, largest thermal station, thermal station → state
natural targets: labour-intensive industries (textiles, IT/ITES, handlooms), clusters and their states
first crude pipeline, rail electrification share by a date, Vande Bharat facts, end-points of trans-continental railways
destination of an export from an Indian port (Vizag iron ore → Japan); natural targets: major ports and their main cargo

traps.trap: Moves a field or region to another state or continent
traps.spot: Lists of oil fields or steel regions with one outsider
traps.fix: Assam: Digboi, Naharkatiya, Moran; Gujarat: Kalol, Ankleshwar; Ruhr is in Germany (Western Europe)
traps.pyq: Kalol not in Assam → I, II, IV [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#118]; 'Ruhr : Eastern Europe' wrong → I, II, IV [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#114]

traps.trap: Reverses a climatic condition behind a crop advantage
traps.spot: 'high temperature disparity' as a reason for tropical cane
traps.fix: Tropical India has an equable climate (low range), long sunshine and cool clear nights; that raises cane yield and sucrose

traps.spot: 'X is not suitable for' in a negative statement list
traps.fix: Wheat grows in the Ganga–Satluj plains and the black-soil Deccan (MP, Maharashtra)

traps.trap: Inflates a rank or a number by one step
traps.fix: India is 2nd in vegetables and fruits (after China) and 2nd in steel; Vande Bharat design speed 180, operating 160 km/h
traps.pyq: vegetables 'biggest' wrong [group1-prelims-2019-paper2#101]; 250 kmph wrong → I, II, IV [group1-prelims-2023-paper2#107]

traps.trap: Swaps regional names of shifting cultivation
traps.spot: Match list of local names and regions
traps.fix: Ladang – Indonesia/Malaysia; Milpa – Central America; Roca – Brazil; Masole – Central Africa; Jhum – NE India

traps.trap: Puts a mineral-based industry among agro-based ones
traps.fix: Classify by raw material: cement (limestone) is mineral-based; cigarettes, vanaspati, paper are agro/forest-based

traps.trap: Offers a neighbouring district for an AP plantation
traps.fix: Coffee is mainly in the agency areas of erstwhile Visakhapatnam (Araku, Paderu) and East Godavari

techniques.name: Raw-material classification
techniques.how: Name the raw material of each industry (crop, forest, mineral, fuel) before reading what the stem excludes.
techniques.example: Tobacco, oilseeds, bagasse/wood [...] are farm or forest inputs; limestone is mineral → Cement [group1-prelims-2008#71]

techniques.name: Match-list anchor on the famous pair
techniques.how: Fix the iconic pair (Jamshedpur – steel, Perambur – ICF), then test which codes keep it.
techniques.example: a-II and d-I leave only 'II III IV I' [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#71]

techniques.name: Firsts and chronology
techniques.how: For 'first' items, recall the earliest project of the type and its era; later projects in the options fall.
techniques.example: Naharkatiya–Nunmati–Barauni (1960s) predates HBJ gas, Jamnagar–Loni LPG and Mumbai High lines → option 3 [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#101]

techniques.name: Geographer–method pairing
techniques.how: Link each regionalisation method to its originator: Weaver – crop combination (Doi modified it); Bhatia – concentration/diversification; Kendall – productivity ranking.
techniques.example: Weaver, Doi = crop combination and Kendall = productivity give 'I II III IV' [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#97]

techniques.name: Joint-author completeness check
techniques.how: When one option names both scholars of a joint work, the single-name options are incomplete.
techniques.example: Four macro agricultural regions were drawn jointly → 'Sengupta and Sdasyuk' [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#104]

techniques.name: Date-stamp production and infrastructure figures
techniques.how: For electrification, plant size or producer rank, recall the figure for the date in the stem only.

confusions.remember: NE fields vs Cambay basin fields
Liquefied petroleum gas vs compressed natural gas
Learn the real locations; the 2023 key on this pair is disputed
Muga is golden silk endemic to Assam
Jute on the Hugli banks; Damodar = coal and steel
Higher yield and sucrose vs larger area
Indonesia vs Central America vs Brazil vs Central Africa
Vande Bharat started as 'Train 18' from ICF

anchors: India is 2nd in world fruits and vegetables (China 1st); UP leads wheat
West Bengal – largest rice producer; Karnataka – ragi; Gujarat – groundnut; Maharashtra – jowar
Wheat regions: Ganga–Satluj plains and black-soil Deccan
Assam oil: Digboi, Naharkatiya (SW of Digboi), Moran
Vande Bharat (Train 18): ICF Chennai, design 180 km/h, operating 160 km/h
Ruhr – Germany; Urals – Russia; Pittsburgh/Atlantic coast – USA
Vizag iron ore exports historically to Japan
checklist: Classify the item first: crop, raw material type, fuel, or transport mode
Place each named field, plant or region on the map – does any belong to another state/continent?
For ranks, check whether India is 1st or 2nd and in what (output, yield, area)
For climate–crop statements, test each condition's direction
For match lists, fix the most famous pair and eliminate codes
Date-stamp any production, capacity or percentage figure
